sources.entry: FSNotes - Notes manager for macOS/iOS: modern notational velocity (nvALT) on steroids.

summary.one_liner: FSNotes is a native notes app for macOS and iOS that stores every note as portable Markdown or plain-text files.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes FSNotes as a fast, native notes app for macOS and iOS with a focused writing experience. Notes are kept as Markdown or plain-text files rather than in a proprietary database, so other apps can open them. It supports multiple folders, external editors, iCloud Drive, Dropbox, and optional Git backups. It adds tags and [[links]] between notes, AES-256 encryption for private notes, and rendering of code, Mermaid diagrams, and MathJax. The README says search and navigation stay smooth across collections of 10,000+ notes. It is written in Swift 5.
use_cases: take and organize Markdown notes on a Mac
keep plain-text notes synced through iCloud Drive or Dropbox
link related notes with tags and wiki-style links
version notes with optional Git backups
write notes with Mermaid diagrams or MathJax formulas
how_to_run: Buy FSNotes from the App Store, which the README says provides regular updates
notable: Notes stored as plain Markdown or text files, not a proprietary database
Works with iCloud Drive, Dropbox, and optional Git backups
caveats: Paid app distributed through the App Store, per the README
README does not describe build or install steps for building from source
